themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints skyrocketed to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 4700% spike—suggesting a sudden, concentrated problem with unlicensed signage, posters, or advertisements across Central Harlem that warrants immediate investigation into what's being posted and by whom.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (4700% increase, z-score: 17.76)
Statistically extreme outlier indicating new, concentrated activity rather than baseline noise
No contextual news reports yet, suggesting this is under-covered
reporting_angles: Canvas affected blocks to determine what is being posted (political ads? construction? promotions?) and identify any patterns
Interview 311 complaint filers to understand why they suddenly began reporting this week

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge This Week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 7 this week compared to a baseline of 0.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—an 833% spike—indicating a potential coordinated tagging campaign or breakdown in sanitation response in Central Harlem.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (833% increase, z-score: 5.74)
Concurrent with illegal posting spike, suggesting possible broader street disorder trend
Gothamist coverage on seasonal pest issues may reflect broader environmental neglect
reporting_angles: Map this week's graffiti complaints to identify geographic clusters or hotspots
Interview NYC Parks or DSNY to determine if staffing or enforcement changed recently

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment-related complaints surged to 15 this week versus a baseline of 4.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 216% spike—aligning with longstanding community board budget requests for homeless facilities upgrades and signaling acute homelessness pressure in Central Harlem.
evidence: 15 encampment complaints this week vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (216% increase, z-score: 3.38)
Community Board has requested homeless facility upgrades for multiple years, indicating chronic underinvestment
Aligns with seasonal warming trend and citywide homelessness patterns
reporting_angles: Identify specific encampment locations from 311 data and visit to assess conditions, services availability, and resident needs
Interview Department of Homeless Services and local outreach providers about capacity and response protocols
Connect to community board's repeated budget requests—why haven't facilities been upgraded?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 7 last week versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1300% spike—suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown, new illegal vending activity, or complaint surge against street vendors in Central Harlem.
evidence: 7 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1300% increase, z-score: 6.5)
Suggests either aggressive enforcement action or surge in unlicensed vending activity
Part of broader street disorder pattern (illegal posting, graffiti, vendor issues converging)
reporting_angles: Interview local street vendors about enforcement pressure, licensing barriers, and economic impact
Determine whether NYPD or DOE has increased enforcement activity or received new directives
Assess whether vendor complaints reflect community safety concerns or economic displacement tensions

themes_detail.label: Missed Garbage Collection Spike
themes_detail.summary: Missed sanitation collection complaints rose to 11 last week versus a baseline of 2.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 389% spike—indicating potential service gaps or staffing issues with NYC's Sanitation Department in Central Harlem.
evidence: 11 missed collection complaints last week vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (389% increase, z-score: 3.75)
Part of broader sanitation/street conditions pattern alongside graffiti and illegal posting spikes
Community board has requested new maintenance equipment, suggesting systemic infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if collection schedule changed, staff shortages occurred, or vehicle breakdowns affected this week
Canvas affected blocks to determine extent of uncollected refuse and any public health concerns
Tie to community board's equipment budget request—is this symptomatic of aging infrastructure?
